plugins.name: plumb
plugins.description: Keep every project true to its sources. A portable framework that defines where project knowledge lives (the KB structure) and keeps it true and current (CI gates, single sources of truth, and one end-of-session ritual).

skills.name: plumb-audit
skills.description: On-demand audit of docs→code drift — walk the doc spine's checkable claims (open/done roadmap items, inventory counts, status fields in queue/data files) against the actual codebase, report a drift table, and correct confirmed findings. The inverse of closeout — closeout asks "what did this conversation produce?"; the audit asks "is what the docs assert still true of the code?". Use when the user says "/plumb-audit", "audit the docs", "verify the docs/roadmap against the code", "is the roadmap still true", suspects the docs are stale — and especially BEFORE a "what should we work on next" planning conversation, which is when a stale backlog does the most damage.
headings: plumb audit — are the docs still true of the code?
3. Verify each claim against the code
4. Report the drift table — then STOP

skills.name: plumb-blueprint
skills.description: Build or refresh the project's solution blueprint — a single self-contained HTML page giving a business + technical overview (roles/permissions matrix, ERD, core workflow swimlane, architecture, security posture) to someone who doesn't know the project. Use when the user says "/blueprint", "solution blueprint", "overview pack", "handover doc", asks for a one-page explainer of the whole system, or when plumb-closeout's blueprint axis flags drift in an existing blueprint.
headings: Solution blueprint — the one-page handover artefact

skills.name: plumb-closeout
skills.description: End-of-session doc-sync ritual for sessions that produced substantial work — capture what exists only in this conversation (decisions made or killed, roadmap changes, new conventions, inventory or state changes) into the project's docs before it is lost. Use when the user says "/plumb-closeout" or "/closeout", asks to wrap up or finish after a meaningful chunk of work, or when the session made a decision or established a convention that isn't recorded anywhere yet. Skip it (or say "nothing to record") for trivial sessions — a typo fix or a Q&A session with no repo changes doesn't need the ritual.
headings: Closeout — keep the docs true to the session

skills.name: plumb-init
skills.description: Scaffold or retrofit the CURRENT project with the Plumb doc-sync framework — a five-slot doc spine (CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md core, project-state, changelog, roadmap, decision records), a registry of canonical sources (the plumb line), and CI drift gates where the stack supports them. Use when the user says "/plumb-init" or "set up Plumb", OR asks in their own words to set up project documentation or an AI-context structure for a repo — e.g. "scaffold CLAUDE.md and docs for this project", "set up a docs system so future sessions have context", "organise our scattered docs", "add ADRs and a changelog structure". Works greenfield or mid-project (retrofit maps existing docs into the spine). Do NOT use for one-off edits to an existing doc.
headings: plumb init — stamp a project with Plumb
